headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of their grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry, some utility companies.
news_headline: Governor Signs Legislation to Protect Ratepayers from Data Center Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed a package of legislation aimed at addressing high energy costs for Virginians and ensuring data centers do not drive up costs for families. The legislation includes measures to protect ratepayers from shouldering the cost of new energy infrastructure investments by data centers and other high-load energy customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water authorities to publicly report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, state environmental agencies, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This initiative, championed by Loudoun County Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to provide credible data for public discourse on data center water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes new requirements for data center siting, including mandatory site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate companies.
news_headline: Virginia Policy Shifts Address Data Center Siting and Noise
news_summary: Virginia is implementing comprehensive policies addressing land use for data centers, with legislation now including noise assessments. HB153 and SB94 specifically require proposed facilities to assess expected noise before local approval, reflecting a broader shift in the state's approach to data center development.
